column1: resilient|Able to recover and adapt after difficulty.|A storm bends a young tree.|The resilient tree grows upright again.
meticulous|Very careful about small details.|An artist examines a tiny mistake.|Her meticulous checks catch every missing line.
incognito|With your identity deliberately concealed.|A famous singer puts on a plain hat and sunglasses.|She travels incognito without attracting attention.
persevere|Keep trying despite difficulty.|A guitarist struggles with a chord.|He will persevere until he can play it.
exhilarating|Very exciting and energising.|Friends climb into a roller coaster.|The exhilarating ride leaves them laughing.
reliable|Able to be depended on.|A commuter waits at a bus stop.|The reliable bus arrives on time again.
affordable|Within someone's available budget.|A shopper compares two price tags.|She chooses the affordable jacket.
flexible|Able or willing to change to suit conditions.|A team finds that its meeting room is busy.|Their flexible plan moves the meeting outside.
patient|Able to wait or deal with difficulty calmly.|A child takes time to tie a shoelace.|The patient teacher waits and helps.
confident|Feeling sure of your ability.|A speaker takes a breath before a talk.|She gives a confident introduction.
curious|Eager to learn or find out.|A student notices an unusual insect.|The curious student examines it closely.
considerate|Thoughtful about other people's needs.|Someone is sleeping beside a bright lamp.|A considerate roommate turns the lamp away.
honest|Truthful rather than deliberately misleading.|A cashier gives a customer too much change.|The honest customer returns the extra money.
practical|Useful in real situations.|A roof leaks into a bucket.|A practical repair stops the leak.
convenient|Easy and suitable for a particular purpose.|A traveller carries bags across town.|A convenient station entrance saves a long walk.
urgent|Needing attention very soon.|Water starts spilling from a broken pipe.|The urgent repair cannot wait until tomorrow.
optional|Available but not required.|A class finishes its main task.|The extra puzzle is optional.
accurate|Correct and precise.|A cook checks a measuring scale.|The accurate measurement matches the recipe.
concise|Brief while keeping the important meaning.|A writer faces a long rambling note.|A concise revision keeps only the key points.
clear|Easy to understand.|A traveller looks confused by directions.|A clear map shows exactly where to turn.
specific|Precise and particular.|A customer asks vaguely for a tool.|A specific request names a small flat screwdriver.
relevant|Connected to the matter being discussed.|A detective sorts a pile of papers.|She keeps the relevant clue beside the case file.
consistent|Following a similar standard over time.|A runner marks training days on a calendar.|Her consistent practice builds endurance.
efficient|Achieving a result with little wasted effort.|A worker carries one box per trip.|An efficient trolley carries several at once.
resourceful|Good at finding ways to solve problems.|A camper loses a tent peg.|The resourceful camper uses a suitable branch.
adaptable|Able to adjust to new conditions.|Rain interrupts a planned picnic.|The adaptable group moves into a shelter.
thoughtful|Showing careful consideration.|A friend notices someone struggling with bags.|A thoughtful offer of help makes the trip easier.
generous|Willing to give more than expected.|A baker has extra bread at closing time.|The generous baker shares it with neighbours.
humble|Not acting as though you are better than others.|A winner receives a trophy.|The humble winner thanks the whole team.
sincere|Genuine in feeling or intention.|Two friends talk after an argument.|A sincere apology helps them reconnect.
candid|Honest and direct.|A designer asks for feedback.|A candid friend points out a real problem kindly.
subtle|Not obvious or easy to notice.|Two almost identical paintings hang together.|A subtle colour change alters the mood.
vivid|Very clear, bright or lively.|A dull sketch has barely visible colours.|A vivid painting makes the scene feel alive.
coherent|Connected in a logical, understandable way.|A student sorts scattered story pages.|The coherent story now follows a clear sequence.
versatile|Useful in several different ways.|A cook chooses a single kitchen tool.|The versatile tool peels, slices and grates.
diligent|Working carefully and steadily.|A student starts a difficult assignment.|Diligent checking helps her finish it well.
tenacious|Not giving up easily.|A climber loses a foothold.|The tenacious climber finds another route.
astute|Quick to understand important details.|A shopper studies two offers.|An astute comparison reveals the hidden fee.
articulate|Able to express ideas clearly.|A team struggles to explain a plan.|An articulate speaker makes the plan understandable.
eloquent|Expressive and persuasive in speech or writing.|A speaker prepares a short tribute.|Her eloquent words move the audience.
empathetic|Able to understand another person's feelings.|A friend looks disappointed after a setback.|An empathetic listener gives them space to talk.
skeptical|Not easily convinced without evidence.|Someone shows a miracle-product advertisement.|A skeptical shopper checks the evidence first.
impartial|Not unfairly favouring one side.|Two teams disagree about a result.|An impartial referee applies the same rules to both.
rational|Based on reason rather than impulse.|A buyer feels tempted by a flashy sale.|A rational decision considers the actual budget.
ingenious|Clever and inventive.|A gardener cannot reach a high plant.|An ingenious pulley lowers the pot safely.
prudent|Careful about risks and consequences.|A traveller checks the weather forecast.|A prudent choice includes a raincoat.
pragmatic|Focused on what works in practice.|A team argues about a perfect bridge design.|A pragmatic repair makes the existing bridge usable.
deliberate|Done intentionally and with thought.|An artist studies several possible colours.|A deliberate choice gives the painting a calmer mood.
perceptive|Good at noticing and understanding things.|A host sees a guest sitting quietly.|A perceptive question helps the guest join in.
spontaneous|Done without advance planning.|Friends hear music in a park.|A spontaneous dance makes them smile.
credible|Believable or worthy of trust.|A reporter compares an anonymous rumour with records.|The records support a credible account.
robust|Strong and able to withstand difficulty.|A flimsy bag tears under heavy books.|A robust bag carries the load securely.
viable|Capable of working successfully.|A team compares a costly plan with its budget.|A smaller project is financially viable.
decisive|Able to make decisions firmly.|A captain studies two possible routes.|A decisive choice gets the team moving.
strategic|Planned to achieve a longer-term goal.|A chess player studies the whole board.|A strategic move creates an advantage later.
accountable|Responsible for explaining your actions.|A team discovers a missed deadline.|The accountable manager explains what went wrong.
transparent|Open about actions and decisions.|A club member asks how money was spent.|A transparent report shows the expenses clearly.
systematic|Following an organised method.|A librarian faces unsorted books.|A systematic process sorts them by category.
rigorous|Very thorough and careful.|An engineer checks a new bridge design.|Rigorous testing finds a weakness before construction.
pivotal|Very important to what happens next.|A relay runner reaches the final exchange.|The pivotal handover decides the team's lead.
compelling|Strongly convincing or interesting.|A speaker offers only a vague claim.|A compelling example makes listeners pay attention.
substantial|Large or important in amount or degree.|A tiny repair leaves most damage untouched.|A substantial repair restores the whole wall.
objective|Based on facts rather than personal preference.|Two judges assess a drawing.|Objective criteria help them compare fairly.
sustainable|Able to continue without exhausting resources.|A gardener empties the last water barrel.|A sustainable system collects rainwater for later.
legitimate|Valid or allowed under the relevant rules.|A visitor approaches a restricted entrance.|A legitimate ticket lets the visitor enter.
cohesive|Working or fitting together well.|A team pulls a rope in different directions.|A cohesive team pulls together.
constructive|Intended to help improve something.|A writer receives a harsh crossed-out page.|Constructive feedback suggests a useful next step.
diplomatic|Tactful when dealing with disagreement.|Two colleagues argue over a plan.|A diplomatic reply acknowledges both concerns.
assertive|Expressing needs clearly and respectfully.|Someone keeps interrupting a colleague.|An assertive request asks for time to finish.
persuasive|Able to convince someone.|A volunteer proposes a clean-up.|A persuasive explanation brings more helpers.
proactive|Acting before a problem becomes urgent.|Clouds gather above laundry outside.|A proactive neighbour brings the clothes indoors.
attentive|Paying close attention.|A pupil explains a difficult question.|An attentive teacher listens before answering.
composed|Calm and in control of yourself.|A presenter drops her notes.|She stays composed and continues speaking.
resolute|Firmly determined.|A learner finds a course difficult.|A resolute decision keeps him practising.
cautious|Careful to avoid unnecessary risk.|A walker reaches a slippery path.|A cautious step avoids a fall.
optimistic|Hopeful about a good outcome.|Seeds have just been planted.|An optimistic gardener imagines the coming flowers.
realistic|Based on what is likely or possible.|A beginner plans to read ten books in a day.|A realistic plan starts with one chapter.
ambitious|Having a strong desire to achieve something.|A runner looks at a distant race banner.|An ambitious goal inspires steady training.
modest|Not large or showy.|A family compares a palace with a small home.|Their modest home meets their needs.
remarkable|Unusual enough to deserve attention.|A damaged old clock lies on a table.|Its remarkable restoration surprises everyone.
reluctant|Unwilling or hesitant.|A pupil pauses at the stage entrance.|The reluctant speaker needs encouragement.
ambivalent|Having mixed feelings.|A traveller packs while looking back at home.|She feels ambivalent about moving away.
apprehensive|Worried about what may happen.|A learner waits outside an examination room.|He feels apprehensive before entering.
content|Satisfied with what you have.|A person rests with a book and tea.|She feels content with a quiet afternoon.
grateful|Feeling thankful.|A neighbour helps carry a heavy parcel.|The grateful recipient thanks him.
frustrated|Annoyed because progress is blocked.|A computer freezes during a task.|The frustrated worker takes a short break.
relieved|No longer worried about something.|A traveller searches for a missing ticket.|She feels relieved when she finds it.
nostalgic|Feeling affection for a past time.|An adult opens an old photo album.|The nostalgic memories bring a smile.
poignant|Deeply moving, often with sadness.|Someone finds a letter from an old friend.|The poignant message brings tears and a smile.
exuberant|Full of lively excitement.|A team waits for its result.|Their exuberant celebration fills the room.
serene|Calm and peaceful.|A busy traveller arrives beside a quiet lake.|The serene setting helps her relax.
uneasy|Slightly worried or uncomfortable.|A person notices an unfamiliar noise.|He feels uneasy until he checks the window.
indifferent|Not interested or concerned.|Two friends excitedly discuss a match.|Their indifferent companion prefers a book.
compassionate|Concerned about others' suffering and willing to help.|A runner falls and hurts a knee.|A compassionate rival stops to help.
reassuring|Making someone feel less worried.|A child hesitates before a new class.|A reassuring welcome eases the worry.
awkward|Uncomfortable or difficult to handle socially.|Two people reach for the same seat.|An awkward pause ends with a laugh.
disappointed|Unhappy because expectations were not met.|A family reaches a closed museum.|The disappointed visitors choose another activity.
enthusiastic|Showing strong interest and enjoyment.|A class starts a new experiment.|An enthusiastic student volunteers to help.
appreciative|Showing that you value something.|A team receives a helpful suggestion.|An appreciative reply thanks the contributor.
curiosity|A desire to know or learn.|A child sees a mysterious footprint.|Curiosity leads her to investigate.
integrity|Honesty and strong moral principles.|A worker discovers a mistake that nobody noticed.|Integrity leads him to report it.
empathy|Understanding another person's feelings.|A friend listens to someone who is upset.|Empathy helps her respond with care.
perspective|A particular way of seeing something.|Two people look at a sculpture from different sides.|Each perspective reveals a different shape.
nuance|A small but meaningful difference.|An artist compares two similar shades.|A nuance of colour changes the expression.
inference|A conclusion drawn from evidence.|Wet umbrellas stand beside the door.|The visitor makes an inference that it is raining.
intuition|An understanding or feeling without conscious reasoning.|A chess player pauses over a possible move.|Her intuition suggests looking more closely.
paradox|An apparent contradiction that may reveal a truth.|A person rushes and makes many mistakes.|The paradox is that slowing down helps him finish sooner.
analogy|A comparison used to explain something.|A teacher puts a pump beside a heart diagram.|The analogy helps explain how blood moves.
hypothesis|An idea that can be tested.|A student wonders if light changes plant growth.|Her hypothesis guides an experiment.
evidence|Information that supports or challenges a claim.|A detective finds a muddy footprint.|The evidence helps explain where someone walked.
context|Surrounding information that helps explain meaning.|A person sees the word bat alone.|A cricket scene gives the word its context.
insight|A useful or deep understanding.|A mechanic studies a recurring fault.|A sudden insight reveals the cause.
implication|A possible consequence or suggested meaning.|A bridge is closed for repairs.|One implication is a longer journey to work.
perception|How something is noticed or understood.|Two viewers see different shapes in a cloud.|Their perception of the same cloud differs.
clarity|The quality of being easy to understand.|A diagram is crowded with arrows.|Removing clutter improves its clarity.
confidence|Trust in your ability or judgment.|A learner practises a talk several times.|Practice builds her confidence.
patience|The ability to wait calmly.|Bread rises slowly in a bowl.|The baker's patience allows it enough time.
courage|Willingness to face fear or difficulty.|A nervous learner steps towards a stage.|It takes courage to begin speaking.
progress|Movement towards a goal.|A learner compares old and new drawings.|The improvement shows real progress.
setback|A difficulty that delays progress.|A runner's shoelace breaks during practice.|The setback delays training but does not end it.
achievement|Something accomplished through effort.|A student works on a difficult model.|The finished model is a proud achievement.
opportunity|A favourable chance to do something.|A notice invites beginners to a workshop.|The workshop offers an opportunity to learn.
priority|Something that should be dealt with first.|A cook faces washing-up and a burning pan.|Turning off the heat is the priority.
compromise|An agreement involving concessions.|Two friends want different holiday activities.|Their compromise includes both a hike and a museum.
consequence|A result of an action.|Someone leaves a window open in rain.|A wet floor is the consequence.
obstacle|Something that blocks progress.|A cyclist meets a fallen branch.|The obstacle forces a short detour.
initiative|Taking action without waiting to be told.|A class notices rubbish in its garden.|A pupil takes the initiative to organise a clean-up.
commitment|A promise or dedication to a task.|A volunteer signs up for regular visits.|Her commitment keeps her returning each week.
collaboration|Working together towards a shared goal.|Two builders each hold part of a shelf.|Collaboration helps them fit it safely.
consensus|General agreement within a group.|A team discusses several meeting times.|They reach consensus on Friday morning.
feedback|Information about how something worked or could improve.|A chef asks diners about a new dish.|Their feedback helps adjust the recipe.
strategy|A plan for reaching a goal.|A player studies a difficult puzzle.|A new strategy solves the corners first.
approach|A way of dealing with a task.|A teacher sees that one explanation is confusing.|A visual approach helps the class understand.
solution|An answer to a problem.|A loose door keeps swinging shut.|A doorstop provides a simple solution.
alternative|Another available choice.|A bus is cancelled.|Cycling is an alternative for this short journey.
benefit|An advantage or helpful result.|A street receives more trees.|Shade is one benefit for walkers.
drawback|A disadvantage.|A traveller likes a cheap hotel.|Its distant location is a drawback.
trade-off|A balance in which gaining one thing means giving up another.|A buyer compares a light bag and a stronger heavy bag.|The trade-off is weight against strength.
balance|A suitable distribution between different needs.|A student plans work and rest.|A sensible balance leaves time for both.
boundary|A limit marking what is acceptable or allowed.|A worker receives calls late at night.|A clear boundary protects personal time.
expectation|A belief about what will happen.|A customer sees a picture of a large cake.|The small cake does not match the expectation.
assumption|Something accepted without checking.|A visitor expects a shop to be open.|The locked door challenges that assumption.
uncertainty|A lack of sure knowledge.|A traveller sees two conflicting forecasts.|The uncertainty makes planning harder.
ambiguity|More than one possible meaning.|An arrow appears between two doors.|The ambiguity leaves visitors unsure which to use.
probability|How likely something is to happen.|Dark clouds gather over a picnic.|The probability of rain increases.
accuracy|How closely something matches the truth or correct value.|A scientist repeats a measurement.|Calibration improves its accuracy.
precision|Exactness or fine detail.|A craftsperson measures a tiny part.|Precision helps the pieces fit.
credibility|The quality of being believable or trustworthy.|A report links its claims to reliable records.|The evidence strengthens its credibility.
authenticity|The quality of being genuine.|A curator compares an original painting with a copy.|Careful checks establish its authenticity.
diversity|A range of different kinds.|A garden contains many different plants.|Its diversity attracts different insects.
inclusion|Making people able to participate.|A doorway has only steps.|A ramp improves inclusion for wheelchair users.
accessibility|How easily people can use or reach something.|A reader struggles with tiny text.|Larger text improves accessibility.
simplicity|The quality of being uncomplicated.|A remote control has dozens of confusing buttons.|A clear design brings simplicity.
complexity|Having many connected parts or difficulties.|A mechanic opens a detailed machine.|Its complexity requires careful study.
flexibility|The ability to adapt or change.|A family must change its travel date.|A flexible booking gives them flexibility.
efficiency|Useful results with little wasted effort.|A gardener carries water in many small cups.|A watering can improves efficiency.
responsibility|A duty to act or take care of something.|A pupil agrees to water the class plant.|That responsibility needs regular attention.
accountability|Being answerable for actions and results.|A project misses a milestone.|Accountability means explaining and addressing the failure.
transparency|Openness about how things are done.|A club displays its spending records.|Transparency helps members understand decisions.
sustainability|The ability to continue without exhausting resources.|A community uses water faster than rain replaces it.|Conservation improves sustainability.
appreciate|Recognise the value of or feel thankful for.|A neighbour helps repair a fence.|I appreciate the time you gave me.
clarify|Make easier to understand.|A learner is puzzled by an instruction.|A drawing helps clarify the task.
resolve|Find a solution to.|Two friends disagree about a shared plan.|A calm discussion helps resolve the problem.
prioritise|Decide what needs attention first.|A student has several tasks due.|She will prioritise the nearest deadline.
collaborate|Work together.|Two musicians practise separate parts.|They collaborate on a new song.
adapt|Change to suit new conditions.|A cook runs out of one ingredient.|She adapts the recipe using what is available.
acknowledge|Recognise or admit.|A manager notices a missed email.|He acknowledges the mistake and replies.
consider|Think carefully about.|A buyer looks at several bicycles.|She considers the price and size before choosing.
compare|Look for similarities and differences.|Two phones sit beside their specifications.|The shopper compares their battery life.
contrast|Show how things differ.|Two drawings show a city at dawn and midnight.|The pictures contrast busy and quiet streets.
evaluate|Judge using relevant information.|A teacher examines a project's strengths and weaknesses.|She evaluates the work fairly.
analyse|Examine parts to understand something.|A coach studies the stages of a race.|He analyses where time was lost.
interpret|Explain or understand meaning.|A traveller studies symbols on a map.|She interprets the symbols using the key.
infer|Draw a conclusion from evidence.|An empty cake plate has fresh crumbs.|We infer that someone recently ate the cake.
imply|Suggest without saying directly.|A host looks at the clock and stacks chairs.|The actions imply that the event is ending.
justify|Give a reason supporting a decision.|A team asks why a route was changed.|The road closure helps justify the decision.
demonstrate|Show clearly how something works or is true.|A teacher holds a folded paper model.|She demonstrates how to open it.
illustrate|Explain using an example or picture.|A writer describes a complicated process.|A drawing helps illustrate the steps.
propose|Put forward an idea for consideration.|A group has no plan for the afternoon.|One friend proposes a visit to the park.
suggest|Offer an idea or possibility.|A learner cannot find a useful book.|The librarian suggests a short story collection.
recommend|Say that something is suitable or worthwhile.|A traveller asks for a quiet café.|A local recommends one near the library.
request|Ask for something.|A guest needs another blanket.|She requests one at reception.
respond|Reply or react.|A teammate asks for help.|He responds with a useful explanation.
negotiate|Discuss to reach an agreement.|A buyer and seller discuss a price.|They negotiate a price both can accept.
persuade|Convince someone to think or act differently.|A friend hesitates to join a walk.|A pleasant route helps persuade her.
encourage|Give support or confidence.|A beginner struggles with a new skill.|A friend's kind words encourage another attempt.
support|Help someone or something.|A learner balances on a bicycle.|A parent supports the bicycle until she is steady.
contribute|Give something towards a shared purpose.|Several neighbours prepare a picnic.|Each person contributes a dish.
participate|Take part.|A class gathers for a discussion.|Everyone can participate by sharing an idea.
improve|Make or become better.|A writer revises an unclear paragraph.|The changes improve its clarity.
refine|Improve through small careful changes.|An artist adjusts a nearly finished sketch.|She refines the details around the eyes.
simplify|Make less complicated.|A recipe has too many unnecessary steps.|The cook simplifies the instructions.
expand|Make or become larger.|A library receives new shelves.|It expands its children's section.
reduce|Make smaller or less.|A household notices wasted electricity.|Switching off unused lights reduces waste.
maintain|Keep in good condition or at a certain level.|A cyclist oils a dry chain.|Regular care maintains the bicycle.
preserve|Protect from damage or loss.|A museum stores an old letter carefully.|The case helps preserve the paper.
restore|Bring back to a previous good condition.|A worn chair has loose joints.|A craftsperson restores the chair.
recover|Return towards a normal state after difficulty.|A runner rests after a hard race.|Time and rest help her recover.
prevent|Stop something from happening.|Rain approaches an uncovered picnic.|A shelter prevents the food getting wet.
anticipate|Expect and prepare for.|A station worker sees a busy holiday approaching.|Extra signs anticipate travellers' questions.
mitigate|Make a harmful effect less severe.|A town prepares for heavy rain.|Sandbags help mitigate flood damage.
alleviate|Make a problem or discomfort less severe.|A person rests in a hot room.|Opening a window may alleviate the heat.
exacerbate|Make a problem worse.|A small argument becomes louder.|More accusations exacerbate the conflict.
implement|Put a plan into action.|A team agrees on a recycling scheme.|They implement it by placing labelled bins.
coordinate|Organise people or activities to work together.|A group prepares a community meal.|One organiser coordinates the cooking times.
delegate|Give someone responsibility for a task.|A leader has too many jobs.|She delegates the invitations to a teammate.
monitor|Watch or check over time.|A gardener checks a new plant each day.|He monitors its growth.
assess|Judge the condition, value or importance of.|A mechanic examines a damaged bicycle.|She assesses what needs repair.
verify|Check that something is true or correct.|A traveller checks a ticket against a timetable.|He verifies the departure time.
confirm|Establish or state that something is correct.|Two friends arrange a meeting.|A message confirms the time and place.
corroborate|Support a statement with additional evidence.|A witness describes a visitor.|A photograph corroborates the account.
challenge|Question or test something.|A student finds a claim without evidence.|She challenges it with a thoughtful question.
reconsider|Think about a decision again.|A walker sees a storm ahead.|He reconsiders the mountain route.
reflect|Think carefully about an experience.|A learner reviews a completed project.|She reflects on what she could do differently.
